newsitem.title: CHINA: China Strike Hard crime crackdown nets 358,000.
newsitem.headline: China Strike Hard crime crackdown nets 358,000.

text.p: China's nationwide "Strike Hard" battle against crime brought 358,000 cases before the courts between April and November, officials and state media said on Tuesday.
People's courts across China would persist with the crackdown next year to safeguard social stability, Ren Jianxin, president of the Supreme People's Court, said here on Tuesday.

"The unified and intensified campaign on cracking down on crimes this year has beaten down the arrogance of criminals, reversing poor public security in some places," the Xinhua news agency quoted Ren as telling a meeting of presidents of provincial Higher People's Courts.
From April to November, China's courts had dealt with 358,000 criminal cases resulting from Strike Hard, with verdicts already reached in 85 percent of those, Ren said.
China announced more than 166,000 arrests in the first three months of the campaign, along with several thousand executions that followed sentencing within days of arrest.
Authorities executed eight people in central China for robbing and murdering 11 drivers of taxis or goods vehicles, the Henan Legal Newspaper seen in Beijing on Tuesday said.
The eight were executed after their appeals were rejected, it said.

"It is a long-term, strategic task of the people's courts to carry forward forceful crackdown on crimes that jeopardise public security and undermine economy, and to go all out to safeguard social stability with utmost efforts," Ren said.
He particularly urged the courts to combat violent, gun-related and organised crimes, pornography, gambling, drugs crimes, prostitution and kidnapping and the sale of women.

China's courts handled more than 4.69 million cases in the criminal, civil, economic, administrative and maritime fields from January to November this year, a rise of 16.33 percent over last year, Ren said.
Of these, verdicts had been reached in more than 4.36 million, an increase of 16 percent from last year, he said.

"Through their trials, the people's courts have made new contributions to guaranteeing (China's) reform and opening-up and promoting the smooth progress of the socialist modernization drive," Ren said.
The courts should also strike at embezzlement, bribery and other crimes disrupting economic order, Ren said.
China's judiciary may face a tough task, as Ren stressed last week when he pledged to stamp out wayward law enforcers who lie, cheat, steal, take hostages and kill to protect their interests.
Widespread protectionism in law enforcement agencies was weakening government authority and tarnishing the image of the nation's judicial organisations, Ren said.
